hud.title: Legend
hud.layers.desc: Colour and icon tell the layer. The expected flow is View, State, Service, Model.
hud.boxes.container: Dashed container: a layer. Its classes live inside it.
hud.boxes.class: Class box. Its members are listed inside.
hud.boxes.count: Number on a box: connections with the focus
hud.boxes.inout: ↘ used by, ↗ uses: how many connections reach it and how many leave it
hud.arrows.dir: Arrows go from left to right: the box on the left uses the box on the right.
hud.arrows.count: The number on an arrow is how many references it groups. Click it to read the code.
hud.arrows.violation: Red and dashed: goes against the layer flow.
hud.arrows.flow: Animated purple: data flow from a trace. Data moves from left to right.

hud.deps.chips: Use the chips above the stack to show or hide each kind. The Dart SDK starts folded as a bundle.

hud.zoom.levels: Zoom with the buttons, Ctrl + mouse wheel or the + and - keys. Zoomed out, members fold first, then each layer folds into a container that still lists its classes, and finally the layers regroup into the project folders. Zooming back in unfolds them.

trail.tip.audit: Audit: heat map plus circular dependencies and layer violations
trail.audit.title: Audit
trail.audit.tip.risk: Mix of coupling, size, cycles and layer violations
trail.audit.tip.coupling: How many other classes it is connected to
trail.audit.tip.size: How many members the class has
trail.audit.tip.cycles: Classes that depend on each other in a circle
trail.audit.tip.violation: A {0} class uses a {1} class: the dependency goes against the layer flow
trail.audit.tip.god: God Class by the Lanza and Marinescu rule: very complex (WMC {0}), many foreign attributes (ATFD) and low cohesion (TCC)
trail.audit.legendTip: From cool (little concern) to red (the first place to look)
trail.audit.noCycles: No class depends on itself through others.
trail.audit.noViolations: Every dependency follows the layer flow.
trail.audit.godNote: {0} God Classes by the Lanza and Marinescu rule. Splitting them by responsibility usually lowers their heat.
hud.audit.desc: The flame button paints every box from cool to red by risk, like the hotspot map of CodeScene, and lists the circular dependencies, the layer violations and the hottest classes. Folded containers take the heat of the hottest class inside. Pick Coupling, Size or Cycles to see one factor alone; click a name to open it. The thresholds and the risk weights are the settings "satori.audit.*"; run the analysis again after changing them.
trail.audit.why.god: God Class: complexity {0}, uses {1} foreign attributes, cohesion {2}%
trail.state.title: State management
trail.state.none: No Bloc, Cubit, ChangeNotifier, Notifier or GetX controller found.
trail.state.fragmentedTip: The project manages state in more than one way. Teams usually pick one to keep onboarding and testing simple.
hud.state.desc: A tag next to a class names the state management it uses (Bloc, Cubit, ChangeNotifier, Notifier, GetX), read from what it extends. A pink arrow "observes" goes from a widget to the holder it listens to (BlocBuilder<X>, context.watch<X>(), Provider.of<X>, Get.find<X>); Riverpod providers are not followed. The audit panel lists the approaches in use and warns when more than one is mixed.
